2014_062_040114mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of April 1, 2014 at Troy High School, combining recognition items, five sets of prior minutes, the February 2014 Treasurer's Report and full check register, curriculum and MEAP reports, the 2013-14 budget amendment, a transportation contract award, three first-reading policies, and the Superintendent's goals update. The most consequential item is Personnel 6.A, ratification of the tentative agreement reached March 22, 2014 with the Troy Education Association and ratified by TEA membership March 26, 2014, running April 1, 2014 through June 30, 2015 and providing all teachers and ancillary staff an off-schedule payment for 2013/2014 of $3,250.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 PM, April 1, 2014, Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Pkwy., Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
Outstanding Teacher Award nominees from across the district were honored; three names went to Oakland Schools for the county program - Ann Lenihan (2nd grade, Costello Elementary), Jennifer Taylor (Math, Boulan Park Middle School) and John Morrison (Physics, Troy High School). Mrs. Lenihan was also named the District's overall Teacher of the Year, receiving a free one-year lease of a car donated by the Suburban Collection. The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence funded 77 mini-grants this year, presented by Treasurer Rich Maziasz. Seven teachers received Michigan Schools and Government Credit Union cash grants, presented by Tina Aleshker.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
Minutes of the March 4, 2014 regular meeting, the March 18, 2014 special meeting and workshop, the March 25, 2014 special meeting and special workshop, and the February 2014 Treasurer's Report.

General Fund revenues were amended from $132,348,365 to $133,654,897 (change 1,306,532), driven by State revenue rising from 84,734,723 to 86,197,867 and Federal falling from 3,502,825 to 3,346,213. Amended excess revenues/(expenditures) is (115,841) against 1,617,693 approved, and ending fund balance June 30 moves from 22,606,943 to 21,954,395.

**Business 8.B - Transportation**
RFP 9769 closed February 11, 2014; invitations went to 7 potential bidders with 2 responding, First Student, Inc. (current provider) and Durham School Services. Total bid amounts compared were $2,975,877.26 for Durham and $2,726,029.06 for First Student, an annual cost difference of $257,527.30 in First Student's favor. The resolution authorizes finalizing a contract with First Student for 2014/2015, 2015/2016 and 2016/2017.

**Personnel**
Item 6.A ratifies the TEA tentative agreement of March 22, 2014 (April 1, 2014 through June 30, 2015): a $3,250 off-schedule payment for 2013/2014, two-step advancement onto a new 14-step salary schedule as of July 1, 2014, a Board-paid tax-sheltered annuity contribution during 2014/2015, student instructional days rising from 179 to 181 and teacher work days from 184 to 187, and maintenance of a minimum 12% General Fund Equity Balance with sharing of any balance above 17%. Item 6.B hires Francine Newman as .5 FTE Speech Pathologist, Services Building.

**Other**
First readings of Board Policy C-1402 (Tobacco-Free Schools), G-1005 (Nondiscrimination) and J-2012 (Anti-Bullying); reports on high school math and health textbook recommendations, 2013-2014 MEAP results, and the Superintendent's goals April update.

Agenda packet of the Troy School District Board of Education for the regular meeting held at 7:00 PM on April 1, 2014 at Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Pkwy., Troy, MI 48098. District administration is at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

RECOGNITION. Nominees for the Troy School District Outstanding Teacher Award included Marianne Belleville (Wass), Karen Bush (Schroeder), Lauri Bussell (Martell), Jason Cichowicz (Schroeder), Genia Connell (Leonard), Erin Detmer (Leonard), Lora Herbert (Hill), Stephanie Hyska (Boulan Park), Natalie Jagels (Smith), Lindsay Keegan (Schroeder), Trudi Motzenbecker (Wattles), Kitty Schmidt (Baker) and Amy Wallace (Leonard), among others. Three district nominees were forwarded to Oakland Schools: Ann Lenihan (2nd grade, Costello Elementary), Jennifer Taylor (Math, Boulan Park Middle School) and John Morrison (Physics, Troy High School), chosen by a TEA selection committee. Mrs. Lenihan was also named the District's overall Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year lease of a car donated by the Suburban Collection. The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, an all-volunteer organization, funded 77 grants this year in every school, recognized by Treasurer Rich Maziasz. Seven teachers received Michigan Schools and Government Credit Union cash grant awards, presented by Tina Aleshker.

PRIOR MINUTES. March 4, 2014 regular meeting at Athens High School, called to order at 7:00 p.m. by Vice President Miletti with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Schmidt and Underwood present, President Philippart absent, Superintendent Fowler and roughly 175 audience members attending. Eleven groups and individuals received second-year Spirit of Diversity Awards designed by the Troy Diversity and Inclusion Council, including the Giving Tree Program, the Baker Buddy Program, the Boulan Park LINKS Program, Leonard Cultural Connections, Morse principal Stephanie Miller, the Troy Social Justice Project, and honorable mentions to Smith Middle School science teachers Tracey Kania and Duane Losey, Troy Union teachers and staff, the Oakland ISD Social Justice Project and Dr. Jay Marks, and Jen Hilzinger. Elliot Gold announced the Troy Youth Assistance Dollars for Education raffle. Public comment on teacher contract negotiations came from Caroline Lawson, Katie Hosbach, Christine Russell, Allison Stefanski, Betsy Murphy and TEA president Tony Lucchi. Resolutions: 14-021 consent agenda (Yes 6, No 0, Philippart absent), including a container refuse collection service award and the January 2014 Treasurer's Report; 14-022 personnel, new hire Stacey Newcomb; 14-023 a one-time off-schedule payment for all non-represented employees regularly employed during 2012/2013 except the superintendent; 14-024 closing Bemis Elementary, Schroeder Elementary, Athens High and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2014/2015 with an exception for not more than 25 incoming ninth grade students residing in the Troy High attendance area, plus siblings of Athens students in grades 9-11; 14-025 E-Rate awards as 2014-2015 General Fund expenditures - Windstream PRI phone lines $4,361.40, Blackboard (formerly Edline) web hosting $30,853.16, AT&T long distance $0.0245 per minute, Sprint smartphone service $49.99 per month; 14-026 a 61-passenger school bus with lift from Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) for $88,555.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; 14-027 closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), 8:03 p.m. to 9:14 p.m. Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources Witt reported TEA fact finding rescheduled to March 19, 20 and 21. Student reports covered Athens student government raising $56,411.37 in one week for Desert Angels, wrestler Thomas Keyes placing 5th at State, ACT and MME testing, and three Troy teams (Boulan Park, Smith, Baker) advancing from a 44-team Michigan Science Olympiad regional to the state tournament April 26 at Michigan State University. Adjourned 9:15 p.m.; minutes submitted by Karl D. Schmidt, Secretary.

The March 18, 2014 special meeting at the Troy Center for Transition adopted resolution 14-028, awarding the Bond 2014 network and phone purchase to Hi-Tech Inc. for Extreme Networks data equipment and Shoretel telecommunications equipment in the amount of $1,912,095 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, carried 5-1 with Miletti voting no and Schmidt absent, after public comment from Steve Doyle, Ray Grover, Brian Nufer and Suhail Shabandri. The March 18 workshop reviewed MEAP results, contracted transportation services and policies C-1402 Smoking, G-1005 Nondiscrimination and J-2012 Anti-Bullying. The March 25 special meeting adopted 14-029 (closed session, 7-0), and the March 25 special workshop addressed the superintendent search with MASB representatives Rodney Green and Donna Oser.

PERSONNEL. Item 6.A ratifies the tentative agreement reached March 22, 2014 between the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA, ratified by TEA membership March 26, 2014, covering April 1, 2014 through June 30, 2015. Terms: an off-schedule payment for 2013/2014 of $3,250 for all teachers and ancillary staff; as of July 1, 2014 eligible staff advance two steps onto a new 14-step salary schedule (with protection against base salary at or below 2012/2013); longevity payments unchanged; lane changes only for 2014/2015; a Board-paid tax-sheltered annuity contribution during 2014/2015; student instructional days increasing from 179 to 181 and teacher work days from 184 to 187 in 2014/2015; and maintenance of the General Fund Equity Balance at a minimum of 12% after the 2014/2015 audit, sharing any balance in excess of 17% with teachers and ancillary staff. Item 6.B hires Francine Newman on a probationary contract as .5 FTE Speech Pathologist at the Services Building; B.A. Michigan State University May 1991 and M.A. Wayne State University May 1993 in Communication Disorders, Michigan license renewed June 2013, previously at Beaumont Hospital Royal Oak from October 2004 to March 2014 and Children's Hospital of Michigan from May 1996 to October 2004; resident of Huntington Woods, Michigan.

CURRICULUM. The high school health recommendation, a 2013 edition text, was reviewed against Michigan High School Health Standards and approved by the Troy School District Sex Education Advisory Board on March 4, 2014, with thanks to Mary McDermott, Karyn Schachinger, Karie Dunneback, Lindsay Noble and Lisa Danhoff.

BUSINESS 8.B - TRANSPORTATION SERVICES. Memorandum dated March 12, 2014 from Mark S. Rajter to Superintendent Dr. Barbara A. Fowler; bids reviewed by Transportation Supervisor Dominick Asaro. RFP 9769 closed February 11, 2014 with invitations to 7 potential bidders and 2 responses, First Student, Inc. (current provider) and Durham School Services. Durham priced on an hourly rate and a 4 hour run time while First Student priced per run up to 5.5 hours, so Durham pricing was converted to a 5.5 hour run time. Comparison lines include regular routes at Durham 242.64 adjusted across 31 routes and 179 days for $1,346,409.36 versus First Student 210.44 for $1,167,731.56; special education at 282.70 for $1,163,875.90 versus 251.64 for $1,036,001.88; total home to school $2,574,749.66 versus $2,276,026.96; total summer regular and special education $115,266.60 versus $105,822.00; total monitor expense $135,861.00 versus $143,540.10; total trip expense $150,000.00 versus $200,640.00; total bid amount $2,975,877.26 versus $2,726,029.06, an annual cost difference of $257,527.30 with First Student lower. The memo notes First Student included the impact of the Affordable Care Act in its price and recommends award for the next five years (an initial three years with up to two years renewal) contingent on a contract executed before July 1, 2014, while the resolution authorizes finalizing a contract for 2014/2015, 2015/2016 and 2016/2017.

POLICIES (first readings). C-1402, retitled from Smoking to Tobacco-Free Schools, prohibits tobacco products and non-tobacco nicotine products including e-cigarettes, shisha or hookah use, snus and dissolvable products in all district vehicles, buildings and property and at all school-sponsored events, by any person, 24 hours per day, seven days per week, 365 days per year, excluding physician-prescribed nicotine replacement therapy; adopted February 2, 1999, revised September 2003, April 20, 2010 and February 12, 2014. G-1005 Nondiscrimination cites Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Age Discrimination Act of 1975 and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, expands protected classes to include sexual orientation, gender identity and socioeconomic status, and names the Assistant Superintendent, Human Resources as coordinator at 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098-4799, voice 248.823.4000; adopted July 10, 2007, revised February 12, 2014. J-2012 Anti-Bullying defines prohibited conduct, retaliation and false accusation, reporting, investigation, parent notice, annual reports to the Board, the superintendent as responsible official, and posting requirements, citing Section 219a of the Michigan Penal Code, 1931 PA 328, MCL 750.219a; adopted June 5, 2012, revised March 6, 2014.

SUPERINTENDENT'S GOALS APRIL UPDATE. Five goal areas: Business Services, Human Resources, Bond Election, Student Achievement, and Community/Business Development. Finance staffing history runs from an external consultant review in spring 2013 through the September 2013 resignation of the Director of Finance, unsuccessful director postings in October 2013 and January 2014, the hiring of an Accounting Coordinator, and payroll and accounting assistant postings with a goal of positions filled by 7-1-14. Data processing followed a county-wide ISD software RFP whose first attempt was terminated during summer 2013 and whose second process began September 2013 with earliest implementation estimated at July 2015; Troy instead upgrades to eFinancePlus version 5.0, with a SunGard user conference in October 2013, a business process review in April 2014, parallel runs against version 4.3 in June 2014 and go-live July 21, 2014. Operations and maintenance moved to SchoolDude software in 2013, used by more than 6,000 educational institutions, with work orders solely in SchoolDude starting the week of April 7-11, 2014 and iPad deployment to maintenance techs in phase 2. Bond slides cite passage with 70% voter approval in every precinct with a record turnout of 13,382 votes cast and a 60% absentee passage rate, alongside earlier results of 52% with 7,195 votes cast, 60% in June 1997 with 5,691 votes cast, and an 82% absentee rejection in June 2004. The 2014 bond project timeline lists design completions between 2/21/14 and 5/23/14, construction starts between 4/23/14 and 8/6/14, completions between 8/29/14 and 8/29/15 (Schroeder), technology phone and network work over Spring Break 2014, track replacement and lighting and auditorium updates in summer 2014, and bus replacement complete by 5/1/14. A committee of 8 principals with curriculum coordinators, Dr. Machesky and Mrs. Keeling investigated NWEA and ACT Aspire and recommended continuing the ACT in 11th grade and administering ACT Aspire in grades 8 and 10. All 4th and 5th grade teachers participated in ELA teacher labs, with TLL and Ellen Cale pilots each involving 12 teachers, and math support classes providing an additional 3 hours of instruction per week for middle school students. Community and business partnerships listed include APT to Succeed, Friends of the Rouge and the Troy Nature Center, the Troy Historical Museum, Consumer Insights at Baker, General Motors with TSD Robotics Team #226 Hammerheads, A World in Motion at Larson with the Society of Automotive Engineers, Troy Beaumont Project Search, Women of Tomorrow, Terrace Cafe with Sodexo, and the Troy Optimist Club Bounty in a Backpack at Morse.
